priceSnapshot.note: The perpetual is 78,680.7 and UP 1.31 percent on the rolling 24h close of 77,662.5. This report is the first session written since 2026-08-28 midday - the 28 August endday and all four 29 August sessions did not run, so the comparison window is 43 hours rather than the usual overnight gap, and the wallet has been unmarked across it. Two things happened in that window. First, the Warsh flush held: the 76,847.3 low printed on 28 August was never revisited and the recovery off it has been steady rather than violent. Second, the 78,160.0 ADD gate written at 28 August midday CONFIRMED - the 1H bar opening 2026-08-29T21:00Z closed 78,192.3 and the next closed 78,194.6 - and price has since extended 486.1 points beyond it, breaking to 78,819.8 on the 12:00Z bar this morning. Price now sits above ALL FOUR EMAs on ALL FOUR timeframes, which has not been true at any point in this log's recent window.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE below $78,080.0 AND a failure to reclaim it on either of the next two hourly bars. This is the base the breakout came from - the 1H bars between 2026-08-30T05:00Z and 11:00Z built a shelf whose lows ran 78,084.0, 77,916.0, 77,952.0, 78,001.6 - so a settled close beneath it says the break was a liquidity grab rather than a trend leg. NOTE ON WIDTH: at 600.7 points this gate is 2.54 hourly ATRs away, far outside the 0.4-to-0.6 band every gate in this log has used. That is deliberate. Hourly ATR has COLLAPSED to 236.57 from the 648.46 recorded at 28 August midday, a 63.5 percent contraction, and 0.4-to-0.6 ATRs now spans only 95 to 142 points - roughly one bar's noise, which would whipsaw on any ordinary pullback. When ATR contracts this hard the band stops being the right tool and structure has to carry the gate instead.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE above $78,830.0, which clears this morning's 78,819.8 session high by 10.2 points. Spot is 149.3 points below it, 0.63 hourly ATRs - inside the usual band, because on the upside the nearest structure happens to sit where the band wants it. A settled close above the high says the breakout is extending rather than fading into the weekend, and opens the 79,860.0 pre-flush high as the next objective.

decisionBox.changed: Bias flips from 28 August midday's BEARISH to BULLISH and the box from REDUCE to ADD. Three things drove the flip. The 78,160.0 add gate written that session fired on a settled 1H close and CONFIRMED on the next bar, which is the cleanest gate confirmation in this window. The 77,480.0 reduce gate from the same session triggered twice - the 22:00Z close of 77,385.3 and the 03:00Z close of 77,475.0 - and was VOIDED both times under the two-bar reclaim rule, the first genuine double-void in the log. And price has moved from below three of four 1H EMAs to above all four on every timeframe. The stop reference moves up to 77,900.0, just under the 77,916.0 shelf low, and is flagged NOT recommended as a resting order because morning is only about six hours away and the wallet carries no leverage to protect.

liquidityMagnet.note: Pull is DOWN despite the bullish price structure, and the two are not in conflict. The OKX retail long/short ACCOUNT ratio is 1.21, up from the 1.16 recorded at 28 August midday and up from roughly 0.92 during the Warsh flush itself, so retail has been adding longs the whole way up. Funding is positive at 0.0042 percent per 8h, meaning longs are paying to hold. The crowded side is therefore the long side, and the deeper pool of forced flow sits beneath the market even while price makes highs. That is the standard shape of a breakout that is vulnerable to one sharp shakeout before it extends - it argues for spot rather than leverage here, not for fading the move.

calibration.rollingRecord: Eighteen sessions logged. The 0.4-to-0.6 ATR band tally now reads three clean confirmations, two whipsaws, one gate that whipsawed then confirmed on the second trigger, and - new this session - one gate that triggered TWICE and was voided BOTH times. That last outcome is the important one, because it is the first case where the sequence-of-triggers heuristic proposed at 28 August midday would have been actively harmful.
calibration.note: The 77,480.0 REDUCE gate from 28 August midday fired twice and was voided twice. Trigger one came at the 2026-08-29T03:00Z close of 77,385.3; the next two bars closed 77,346.7 and then 77,728.1, a clean 248.1 points back above the line, voiding it on bar two. Trigger two came at the 2026-08-29T09:00Z close of 77,475.0 - just 5.0 points through - and the very next bar closed 77,615.6, voiding it on bar one. Against the current 78,680.7, acting on either trigger would have sold 1,295.4 and 1,205.7 points too low respectively, so acting_helped is FALSE and the two-bar reclaim rule did exactly the job it exists for. The ADD gate at 78,160.0 DID fire and confirm: the 2026-08-29T21:00Z bar closed 78,192.3 and the 22:00Z bar closed 78,194.6, and price is now 486.1 points beyond it. Acting on the add was correct. Two findings worth carrying. First, the sequence heuristic from last session - treat a voided first trigger as an early probe rather than a wrong level - would have produced a bad trade here, so it needs a qualifier: it applies when the second trigger runs FURTHER through the level, not when it barely clips it, and trigger two at 77,475.0 was only 5.0 points through. Second, this run had no 28 August endday and no 29 August sessions to grade against, so a 43-hour gap was assessed in one step; gates written for a 7-hour horizon should not be assumed to still be live across a gap that long, and the fact that both reduce triggers landed INSIDE the unmonitored window is the reason they went ungraded until now.
